idiom_name: MikroORM inheritance: 'tpt' on the root entity
implementation_notes: MikroORM is the mainstream JavaScript ORM with a first-class joined strategy: setting inheritance: 'tpt' on the root entity gives each class its own table, makes the child table's primary key a foreign key to the parent with ON DELETE CASCADE, and joins the path when hydrating objects. What replaces the classic mapper is ORM metadata plus the identity map, so a find on the base returns concrete subtypes without hand-written joins. A hand-written join over the same schema stays justified for a single hot query or when the project runs without an ORM.
pitfalls: Deleting a base row without the cascade leaves child rows behind, and a later load half-populates the object; MikroORM sets ON DELETE CASCADE for tpt, hand-written schemas must state it themselves.
One table per class turns each subclass load into a join; fetching child rows per parent instead of populating the path produces the classic N+1 query storm.

variants.name: Hand-written SQL joins with per-type row mappers
variants.idiom_name: raw join query plus a row-to-object function per class
variants.implementation_notes: Without an ORM the schema is still the pattern: one table per class, subclass key = foreign key, and a loader per type that runs the join and maps the row to an object (pg, knex or better-sqlite3). What replaces the classic mapper is that explicit loader plus a type column for polymorphic reads, and writes go inside BEGIN ... COMMIT so the tables of the path stay in step. Choose it when the schema is owned elsewhere or a single hot path makes ORM hydration the bottleneck.
pitfalls: A join that forgets the child table yields undefined subtype fields, and JSON.stringify turns undefined into null - silent data loss instead of an error.
Each loader repeats the join text, so a changed schema drifts between the read and write paths; keep the SQL for a type in one module.
